source.title: Revealing the structure of language model capabilities
source.authors: Ryan Burnell; Hank Hao; A. Conway; José Hernández Orallo

record.tranche_reason: The study uses factor analysis rather than loss-versus-scale sweeps, and reports correlations between model size and performance factors that bear on whether performance relates to scale.
record.gate_note: The study reports correlations between model characteristics and latent performance factors. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute; fit scaling laws; test extrapolation; or test compute-optimal allocations. Cited scaling-law findings are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: Across 29 HELM models, the study correlates log parameter count with latent benchmark-ability scores. This bears on whether downstream performance improves with scale (V6). The models are uncontrolled: families, data and tuning all differ. No loss curves or fits are reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors say they found support for scaling laws, since all three factors correlate positively with size. Scale relates most strongly to comprehension, which they suggest explains inconsistent task-level scaling findings. Instruction tuning has divergent associations, and they found no clear token relation, given limited token variation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses factor analysis of HELM benchmark performance and correlations with model characteristics, rather than measuring held-out loss across model, data, or compute scales.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors caution that factor-analysis results depend on task selection and note that interpretations of factors are partly subjective.

fits_no_version.finding: Instruction tuning correlates negatively with language modeling (-0.50), positively with reasoning (0.44), and non-significantly with comprehension.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instruction tuning shifts broad abilities in divergent directions.

fits_no_version.finding: No clear relation between training-token totals and any factor, with little token variation in the sample.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this sample, training tokens do not track the latent abilities.

record.problems: The sample includes only 29 models, and the frequentist factor model has somewhat poor fit (CFI = 0.70, TLI = 0.61, RMSEA = 0.26). The authors note limited variation in training lengths, subjective factor interpretation, and dependence of the factor structure on the tasks included.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported outcomes directly test the versions of the claim. Factor loadings, factor scores by individual model, task correlations, and figures about factor structure do not measure a scaling law or compute-optimal allocation.

untested.parts: Prediction from pretraining loss; out-of-sample or extrapolated prediction; functional form of the scale–performance relation; controlled within-family scaling.
Not tested: no loss-versus-parameters, tokens or compute sweep or fit.
Not tested: no other modalities or regimes.
Not tested: no comparison of exponents or fitting choices.

missing.what: Per-model factor scores showing large models with low reasoning (BLOOM 176B -0.01, OPT 175B -0.33) while InstructGPT davinci scores 3.58. Also, InstructGPT ada has the lowest language-modeling score (-4.00). These bear on how predictable V6's scale effect is.
Scatter plots of log size against each factor with linear fits.

record.verdict_notes: Small sample (29 models), poor frequentist fit (RMSEA 0.26), heterogeneous model families. The size correlations are confounded by family, data and tuning, so they are weak evidence on V6. The language-modeling factor uses bits-per-byte tasks, but no loss-scale relation is reported, so it does not bear on V1.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss, power-law form, parameters/tokens/compute sweeps, and the several-orders-of-magnitude condition.
No small-run fits or predictions for larger runs.
No fixed-compute comparison or loss-minimising parameter/token allocation.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No test of whether a power-law form transfers to other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
The study tests associations between model size and latent benchmark-performance factors, not downstream performance predictions from pretraining loss or out-of-sample prediction.
No comparison of scaling-law exponents, fitting choices, or departures from a single power law.

rows.subject: 29 LLMs (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Correlated log model size with the comprehension factor score
rows.measure: Pearson correlation with log model size
rows.note: Aggregate association across the included models; this is not a fitted scaling law.
rows.check: Correct. r=0.70 with log size, the strongest of the three factors. It is a cross-family correlation, not a scaling curve.

rows.subject: 29 LLMs (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Correlated log model size with the language modeling factor score
rows.measure: Pearson correlation with log model size
rows.note: Aggregate association across the included models; the factor is based on benchmark next-token prediction tasks, not a loss-versus-size curve.
rows.check: r=0.49, CI [0.16, 0.72]: positive but much weaker than comprehension. The authors stress that scale is not uniformly related to the abilities. The factor is built from bits-per-byte tasks, but it is a factor score, not loss, so it does not bear on V1.

rows.subject: 29 LLMs (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Correlated log model size with the reasoning factor score
rows.measure: Pearson correlation with log model size
rows.note: Aggregate association across the included models; this is not a fitted scaling law.
rows.check: r=0.51, CI [0.19, 0.73]: moderate and weaker than comprehension. Figure 2 shows 175B+ models such as BLOOM and OPT near the bottom on reasoning.

source_check.correct: The correlation and interval are correct. In Figure 2, BLOOM ranks seventh of 29 on reasoning; the two OPT entries rank fourteenth and twenty-first.
source_check.locator_found: Table 3; Section 3.5; Figure 2, sorted by reasoning score.
source_check.problem: The verdict-fix gloss incorrectly describes BLOOM as near the bottom on reasoning.

source_check.label: supports

relationships.condition: Language-modeling and reasoning factors across the same models
relationships.reason: Correlations are only moderate (0.49, 0.51; R2, R3), and scale relates unevenly to abilities. Figure 2 shows some 175B models scoring low on reasoning.
relationships.display_finding: Correlations were only 0.49 and 0.51, and some 175B models still scored poorly on reasoning.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Language-modeling and reasoning factors across the same models
source_check.reason: R2 and R3 show weaker positive associations, 0.49 and 0.51. Sections 3.5 and 4 explicitly conclude that scale relates unevenly to these abilities; this qualifies uniform predictability without showing an absent or reversed aggregate effect.
